meta.name: Normative knowledge graph for cross-border health-data transfers
meta.scope: A bounded decision-support graph for the 15 GDPR/HIPAA checklist items and selected Irish implementing rules. It is not a complete legal ontology or a certification of a transfer. Route core statements and explicit conditions must both hold. Source law, interpretive guidance, and intake/evidence policy are distinct.

requirement_roles.applicability: Decides whether a regime applies at all; every other requirement of that regime is gated by it. 'unmet' means the regime does not apply, never a violation.
requirement_roles.obligation: Something that must hold for the transfer under an applicable regime.
requirement_roles.national: A Member State provision that supplies a GDPR reference to national law (an opening). Reached only through implemented_by.

condition_kinds.scope: A factual classification that decides whether a requirement or condition arises, or whether an exception displaces it. Never reported as unmet.
condition_kinds.substantive: Something that must be true or in place; can be unmet.

units.transfer: Owed for each transfer or disclosure and assessed on the one described (the default when a requirement declares no unit).
units.activity: Owed once for the processing activity, or by the regulated entity, that a transfer belongs to. A single transfer within an existing activity relies on it rather than re-establishing it; the unit's basis quotes the text that attaches it to the activity.

conditions.statement: Personal data are processed (automated or filing-system processing) and no Art. 2(2) exclusion applies. Pseudonymised data remain personal data; anonymous information is outside the Regulation.
The parties jointly determine the purposes and means of the processing.

Joint-controller responsibilities are transparently allocated and the arrangement reflects the parties' roles and makes its essence available to data subjects, unless and insofar as applicable law determines those responsibilities (Art. 26(1)-(3)).
One party processes the personal data on behalf of the other.

The relevant controller/processor or processor/subprocessor relationship meets applicable Art. 28 requirements: sufficient guarantees, required prior authorisation for subprocessors, a binding contract or legal act containing the required terms and equivalent subprocessor obligations.

The legal obligation relied on is laid down by Union law or Member State law to which the controller is subject. The legal basis determines the purpose and meets an objective of public interest and proportionality under Art. 6(3).

The public task or official authority relied on is laid down by Union law or Member State law to which the controller is subject. Its purpose is determined in that basis or necessary for the public task/authority, and the law meets public-interest and proportionality requirements under Art. 6(3).
The controller is a public authority processing in the performance of its tasks.
The data include special categories of personal data (here usually data concerning health or genetic data).
The processing is authorised by Union or Member State law, or a collective agreement under Member State law, with appropriate safeguards.
The substantial public interest is set out in proportionate Union or Member State law providing suitable and specific measures. It respects the essence of the right to data protection.
The health or social care processing rests on Union or Member State law, or on a contract with a health professional.

The data are processed by or under the responsibility of a professional subject to an obligation of professional secrecy, or by another person subject to an obligation of secrecy, in either case under Union or Member State law or rules established by national competent bodies (for example a professional regulator's binding rules on confidentiality).
The public-health processing rests on Union or Member State law providing suitable and specific measures, in particular professional secrecy.
The research processing rests on proportionate Union or Member State law providing suitable and specific measures. It respects the essence of the right to data protection.
The processing is for archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes.
Appropriate safeguards are in place: technical and organisational measures ensuring data minimisation, pseudonymisation where the purpose allows, and non-identifying data where it suffices.

A controller or processor subject to the GDPR for this processing makes personal data available to ANOTHER controller, joint controller or processor in a third country, or to an international organisation. The exporter need not be located in the EEA; access within the same legal entity alone does not meet the separate-importer criterion.
Enforceable data subject rights and effective legal remedies are available, assessed against the importer's country's law and practice, with supplementary measures where needed.
The important public interest is recognised in Union law or in the law of the Member State to which the controller is subject.
The exporter is a public authority acting in the exercise of its public powers.

The processing is likely to result in a high risk to individuals (Art. 35(3)(b) lists large-scale processing of special categories; under Recital 91 an individual physician's or other health care professional's processing of patients' data is not large-scale). An individual practitioner is not exempt from every high-risk trigger: consider Art. 35(1), (3)-(5) and applicable supervisory-authority lists.

A DPIA covering this processing is completed before it starts, contains Art. 35(7) assessments and measures, and meets applicable consultation and review requirements under Art. 35(2), (8), (9), (11); an existing activity is covered only if the assessment remains applicable to its current risk.

The relevant controller and processor implement risk-appropriate technical and organisational measures under Art. 32(1)-(4), including assessment, ongoing confidentiality/integrity/availability/resilience, restoration and testing as appropriate. Each actor is assessed for processing for which it is responsible.

The controller meets the applicable Art. 13 or Art. 14 information, timing, further-processing and transfer-information requirements. Information need not be repeated where Art. 13(4) or Art. 14(5) applies; any conditions and alternative safeguards for the particular exception must be met.

The controller facilitates the exercise of data subject rights under Arts. 15-22 (access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, objection). Apply the qualifications in Art. 12(2)-(6), including identification, time limits and manifestly unfounded/excessive requests; the underlying rights have their own scope and exceptions.

The relevant controller or processor keeps records meeting the applicable Art. 30(1)-(4) requirements, unless the narrow Art. 30(5) exemption applies; fewer than 250 employees alone is insufficient where processing is non-occasional, risky, or involves Art. 9 or Art. 10 data.
Retention is limited to what the purposes require (or justified for research under Art. 89(1)).

The information is protected health information: individually identifiable health information, not de-identified under 164.514(a)-(b). A limited data set is still PHI, and coded data are PHI if the re-identification code is disclosed.
The sender is a covered entity or business associate acting in that regulated capacity for this PHI. Country alone does not decide regulated status.
For this transaction the recipient acts on behalf of this sender as its business associate, or as the sender business associate's subcontractor; an unrelated business-associate role does not suffice.

Where 164.502(e) requires assurances for this business-associate/subcontractor relationship, they are documented by a contract or other arrangement meeting the applicable 164.504(e)(2), (3) or (5) terms, including permitted uses, safeguarding and downstream restrictions; apply the express statutory exceptions.

The disclosure relies on the limited-data-set permission under 164.514(e), rather than a different independently valid permission. A dataset classification alone does not establish reliance on that permission.
The data set excludes all sixteen direct identifiers listed in 164.514(e)(2).
The limited data set is used or disclosed only for research, public health or health care operations.
A data use agreement meeting 164.514(e)(4) gives satisfactory assurance that the recipient will use or disclose the data only for limited purposes.
Reasonable efforts limit the PHI disclosed to the minimum necessary for the purpose.
The disclosure is to a health care provider for treatment.

Applicable administrative, physical and technical safeguards, organisational requirements and documentation under 164.306 and 164.308-316 protect electronic PHI; required specifications and the assess/document/alternative-measure rules for addressable specifications are respected.
The recipient is itself a covered entity (or a business associate) holding the information.

The covered-entity recipient has the privacy safeguards required by 164.530(c)(1)-(2), protecting against intentional/unintentional impermissible uses/disclosures and reasonably limiting incidental disclosures.

Processing is necessary and proportionate for a function conferred on this controller by or under an enactment or the Constitution, including administering a non-statutory scheme/programme/funds whose legal basis is such a function (s. 38(1)(a)-(b)); identify that function. Other statutory bases remain possible.
Suitable and specific measures safeguard the data subjects' rights (s. 36 lists examples such as access limits, logging, pseudonymisation and encryption).
The processing is undertaken by or under the responsibility of a health practitioner, or of a person owing an equivalent duty of confidentiality.

The processing is carried out by or under the responsibility of a medical practitioner registered with the Medical Council, to whom the Council's confidentiality standard applies. This alone does not cover persons outside that responsibility.
The controller processes personal data for health research within Reg. 3(2) (scientific research for the purpose of human health).
The health research has ethical approval from a research ethics committee.
The data protection implications have been assessed, with a DPIA where that assessment indicates high risk.

The Reg. 3(1)(a)-(d) measures are in place: necessity arrangements, governance structures (controller, processors, funders and data recipients specified; training), management controls (minimisation, access and logging, security, end-of-research arrangements) and transparency.
Applicable Union or Member State law provides that consent cannot lift the Art. 9(1) prohibition for this processing.
Every Art. 35(10) condition holds: Art. 6(1)(c)/(e) legal basis regulates this operation, a DPIA formed part of adopting that basis, and Member State law does not require a further prior assessment.
The disclosure is to the Secretary in accordance with subpart C of part 160.
The use or disclosure is required by law as described by 164.512(a); it is limited to the relevant requirements of that law.
The use or disclosure is required for compliance with applicable requirements of this subchapter.
The sender acts as a business associate for this use/disclosure.
The sender acts as a covered entity for this use/disclosure.

The business associate's use/disclosure is permitted or required by its governing contract/arrangement or required by law under 164.502(a)(3), complies with applicable 164.504(e) limits and required disclosures under (a)(4), and is not otherwise prohibited.
The relevant processing involves electronic protected health information of a covered entity.
The recipient acts as a covered entity for this PHI.
The recipient acts as a business associate for this PHI.

The recipient business associate complies with its applicable contract/arrangement safeguarding duties under 164.504(e), including preventing uses/disclosures outside the agreement and applicable Security Rule duties.

Any additional Member State conditions applicable to this genetic, biometric or health-data processing are satisfied, regardless of which Art. 9(2) route is used; identify applicable law or establish that no additional condition applies.
The special-category processing is necessary and proportionate for archiving in the public interest, scientific/historical research or statistical purposes under s. 54.
The s. 42 requirements hold: suitable and specific measures, Art. 89 compliance, data minimisation, and non-identifying processing whenever it can fulfil the purpose.
This processing is necessary for one of the medical, occupational-health, health-care, treatment, social-care or systems/services purposes in s. 52(1).
This processing is necessary for public-interest reasons in public health under s. 53, with the relevant need and safeguards established.
The use or disclosure is made to the individual who is the subject of the PHI.
The use or disclosure is made pursuant to a valid authorization under 164.508, with its required contents, scope and validity conditions.

requirements.statement: The GDPR applies: personal data are processed within its material scope and one territorial-scope ground applies.

items.label: Establishment in the Union
items.statement: The particular processing is in the context of the activities of an establishment of the relevant controller or processor in the Union, regardless of where processing occurs. Apply the test to each actor; one party being established does not automatically establish the other party's scope.

items.label: Offering goods or services to people in the Union
items.statement: The relevant controller or processor is not established in the Union; the processing concerns people in the Union and relates to offering them goods or services, whether or not payment is required.

items.label: Monitoring behaviour in the Union
items.statement: The relevant controller or processor is not established in the Union; the processing concerns people in the Union and relates to monitoring their behaviour insofar as it takes place in the Union.

items.label: Member State law applies by public international law
items.statement: The controller is not established in the Union but processes personal data in a place where Member State law applies by virtue of public international law.

requirements.statement: Where the parties are joint controllers or controller and processor, the arrangement those roles require is in place. Independent controllers need neither.
Each controller's processing that is subject to the GDPR (at least the sender's disclosure) has at least one Art. 6(1) basis.

items.label: Consent
items.statement: The data subject has given valid consent to this processing for one or more specific purposes, meeting Arts. 4(11) and 7, including demonstrability, a distinguishable intelligible request, withdrawal and freedom of choice.

items.label: Contract with the data subject
items.statement: This processing is necessary to perform a contract with the data subject or to take steps at that person's request before entering a contract. Merely having a contract is insufficient.

items.label: Legal obligation
items.statement: This processing is necessary to comply with a legal obligation to which the controller is subject. A purpose label alone does not establish that obligation or necessity.

items.label: Vital interests
items.statement: This processing is necessary to protect the vital interests of the data subject or another natural person.

items.label: Public task or official authority
items.statement: This processing is necessary for a task carried out in the public interest or the exercise of official authority vested in this controller.

items.label: Legitimate interests
items.statement: This processing is necessary for a legitimate interest pursued by the controller or a third party, and the data subject's interests or fundamental rights and freedoms do not override it, in particular where the data subject is a child.

requirements.statement: Processing health or genetic data is prohibited unless one Art. 9(2) condition applies.

items.label: Explicit consent
items.statement: The data subject has given valid explicit consent for this processing of these special categories for one or more specified purposes, meeting Arts. 4(11) and 7.

items.label: Employment and social security law
items.statement: This processing is necessary to carry out obligations or exercise specific rights of the controller or data subject in employment, social security or social protection law.

items.label: Vital interests, data subject incapable of consent
items.statement: This processing is necessary to protect vital interests of the data subject or another natural person and the data subject is physically or legally incapable of giving consent.

items.label: Not-for-profit body, members only
items.statement: A body with a political, philosophical, religious or trade-union aim processes the data in its legitimate activities with appropriate safeguards; the data relate solely to members, former members or people in regular contact in connection with its purposes; disclosure outside the body has the data subjects' consent.

items.label: Manifestly made public by the data subject
items.statement: These particular personal data were manifestly made public by the data subject.

items.label: Legal claims or courts
items.statement: The processing is necessary to establish, exercise or defend legal claims, or courts are acting in their judicial capacity.

items.label: Substantial public interest
items.statement: This processing is necessary for substantial public interest reasons; the separate statutory-basis and safeguard conditions also hold.

items.label: Medicine, diagnosis, health or social care
items.statement: This processing is necessary for preventive or occupational medicine, assessing working capacity, diagnosis, health or social care or treatment, or managing health or social care systems and services. A treatment purpose alone does not establish necessity.

items.label: Public interest in public health
items.statement: This processing is necessary for public-interest reasons in public health, such as serious cross-border health threats or high standards of quality and safety of health care, medicines or medical devices.

items.label: Archiving, research or statistics
items.statement: This processing is necessary for archiving in the public interest, scientific or historical research, or statistical purposes. A research label alone does not establish necessity.

requirements.statement: A transfer to a third country complies with Chapter V: an adequacy decision, appropriate safeguards, or a derogation for a specific situation.

items.label: Adequacy decision
items.statement: A currently applicable Commission adequacy decision covers the destination, recipient, data and processing. For the US, verify the recipient's active DPF listing and the certification's scope, including HR-data coverage where relevant.

items.label: Appropriate safeguards (SCCs, BCRs and other Art. 46 tools)
items.statement: An applicable safeguard instrument under Art. 46(2) or an authorised Art. 46(3) arrangement covers the actual exporter, importer and processing, with its required terms and any required authorisation. Naming SCCs or BCRs alone is insufficient.

items.label: Derogation: explicit consent to the transfer
items.statement: Without an adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards, the data subject explicitly consents to this proposed transfer after being informed of its possible risks due to that absence; valid consent requirements also hold.

items.label: Derogation: contract with the data subject
items.statement: Without adequacy or appropriate safeguards, this transfer is necessary to perform a contract between data subject and controller or implement pre-contractual measures taken at the data subject's request.

items.label: Derogation: contract in the data subject's interest
items.statement: Without adequacy or appropriate safeguards, the transfer is necessary to conclude or perform a contract in the data subject's interest between the controller and another natural or legal person.

items.label: Derogation: important reasons of public interest
items.statement: Without adequacy or appropriate safeguards, the transfer is necessary for important public-interest reasons recognised by the applicable Union or Member State law.

items.label: Derogation: legal claims
items.statement: Without adequacy or appropriate safeguards, this transfer is necessary to establish, exercise or defend legal claims.

items.label: Derogation: vital interests
items.statement: Without adequacy or appropriate safeguards, this transfer is necessary to protect vital interests of the data subject or other persons and the data subject is physically or legally incapable of consent.

items.label: Derogation: public register
items.statement: Without adequacy or safeguards, the transfer is from a register intended by law to inform the public and open to consultation under applicable conditions; those conditions hold, the whole register or entire categories are not transferred, and any legitimate-interest access restriction is respected (Art. 49(1)(g), (2)).

items.label: Derogation: compelling legitimate interests (last resort)
items.statement: Neither Art. 45 nor 46 nor any first-subparagraph Art. 49(1) derogation can support the transfer. It is not repetitive, concerns only a limited number of data subjects, is necessary for compelling controller interests not overridden by data-subject interests or rights, and the controller has assessed all circumstances, supplied suitable safeguards, informed the supervisory authority and data subjects, and documented the assessment and safeguards under Art. 49(6).

requirements.statement: Research, archiving or statistical processing is subject to Art. 89(1) safeguards.
Processing likely to result in high risk is preceded by a data protection impact assessment.
Security of processing (an ongoing duty; advisory in the catalogue).
Transparency, data-subject rights, records and storage limitation (ongoing duties; advisory in the catalogue).

The Privacy Rule is engaged: a party to the transfer (sender or recipient) is a covered entity or business associate, and the information is protected health information. Which duties fall on whom is decided by each requirement's scope.

items.label: A party is a covered entity
items.statement: At least one party is a covered entity under 160.103: a health plan, health care clearinghouse, or health care provider transmitting health information electronically in a covered transaction.

items.label: A party is a business associate
items.statement: At least one party is a business associate under 160.103, including a qualifying subcontractor; only provisions made applicable to that role bind it.

requirements.statement: A regulated sender's use/disclosure has permission appropriate to its capacity. Covered-entity permissions and business-associate authority are separately scoped, and all applicable restrictions remain binding.

items.label: To the individual
items.statement: The disclosure is to the individual who is the subject of the PHI under 164.502(a)(1)(i), subject to applicable special restrictions and any mandatory-access rules.

items.label: Treatment, payment or health care operations
items.statement: The covered entity's particular use or disclosure meets 164.506(c): its own treatment/payment/operations, treatment by a provider, another entity's payment activities, qualifying operations with the required relationships and purpose, or an organised health-care arrangement. Psychotherapy-note, marketing, sale-of-PHI and other applicable restrictions still apply.

items.label: Incidental to a permitted disclosure
items.statement: The disclosure is incidental to an otherwise permitted or required use/disclosure and the applicable minimum-necessary and privacy-safeguard requirements in 164.502(b), 164.514(d) and 164.530(c) have been complied with.

items.label: Valid authorization
items.statement: An unexpired, unrevoked authorization satisfies 164.508(b)-(c), including all core elements and statements, signature and date, plain language and applicable compound-authorization/conditioning rules, and covers this use/disclosure; it cannot override an applicable prohibition.

items.label: Agreement or opportunity to object (164.510)
items.statement: This disclosure fits 164.510(a) or (b), including the facility-directory or care/payment/disaster-relief purpose, the permitted recipient and information limits, and the applicable opportunity to agree/object or professional-judgment conditions.

items.label: Disclosure to a business associate
items.statement: The recipient acts on behalf of this sender in a qualifying business-associate or subcontractor relationship under 164.502(e), with satisfactory assurances and terms under 164.504(e). A contract cannot authorise an otherwise impermissible use.

items.label: Other permissions in 164.502 (not modelled)
items.statement: Other uses/disclosures under 164.502 are not fully modelled; this placeholder cannot establish permission.

items.label: Research: IRB or privacy board waiver of authorization
items.statement: The covered entity obtains documentation of an IRB or privacy-board waiver or alteration meeting every applicable condition in 164.512(i)(1)(i) and (i)(2), including privacy risk/protection/destruction/non-reuse assurances, impracticability, identification of necessary PHI, board procedure and signature.

items.label: Research: reviews preparatory to research
items.statement: Representations satisfy 164.512(i)(1)(ii): the use/disclosure is solely to prepare a research protocol or similar preparatory purpose, no PHI is removed from the covered entity by the researcher, and the PHI sought is necessary for that purpose.

items.label: Research on decedents' information
items.statement: Representations satisfy 164.512(i)(1)(iii): the use/disclosure is solely for research on decedents' PHI, the PHI is necessary for the research, and documentation of death is provided if requested.

items.label: Public health activities
items.statement: This use/disclosure fits a specific paragraph of 164.512(b), including its authorised public-health actor or other specified recipient, purpose and any required notice or other conditions. A general public-health purpose alone does not suffice.

items.label: Other 164.512 permissions (not modelled)
items.statement: Other 164.512 permissions are not fully modelled; this placeholder cannot establish permission. The vacated reproductive-health attestation provisions must not be applied merely because they remain printed in eCFR.

items.label: Limited data set with a data use agreement
items.statement: The covered entity uses the 164.514(e) limited-data-set permission for this disclosure; exclusion of the specified identifiers, a permitted purpose and a compliant data-use agreement must all hold.

items.label: Fundraising or underwriting (164.514(f)-(g); not modelled)
items.statement: The 164.514(f)-(g) permissions and their restrictions are not fully modelled; this placeholder cannot establish permission.

items.label: Business-associate contractual or statutory authority
items.statement: The sender is acting as a business associate. Its separate business-associate permission condition must also be met.

requirements.statement: The regulated sender obtains the applicable business-associate or subcontractor assurances under 164.502(e) and 164.504(e); disclosure relying on the limited-data-set permission also requires a data-use agreement.
The disclosure is limited to the minimum necessary, unless an exception in 164.502(b)(2) applies.
Security Rule safeguards (ongoing duties; advisory in the catalogue).
A recipient that is itself regulated safeguards the PHI it receives (advisory in the catalogue).

DPA 2018 s. 38(1) supports processing necessary and proportionate for a statutory or constitutional function, including administering a non-statutory scheme, programme or funds whose administration has that legal basis. It does not itself identify this controller’s particular function.

Irish law permits health-care processing of special categories under Art. 9(2)(h), by or under the responsibility of a health practitioner, with suitable and specific measures. The processing must be necessary for a purpose listed in s. 52(1).

For registered medical practitioners, the Medical Council, which the Medical Practitioners Act 2007 charges with specifying standards of practice and guidance on professional conduct and ethics (s. 7(2)(i)), sets a professional and ethical duty to maintain patient confidentiality (Guide 2024, para. 25.2). Treating that guide as 'rules established by national competent bodies' under GDPR Art. 9(3) is an interpretation, not a statutory statement: the guide says it is not a legal code. Secrecy duties of other professions and statutory duties are not modelled, so failure here does not rule out another source.

Irish law permits processing of special categories for public interest reasons in the area of public health, with suitable and specific measures. The processing must be necessary for the public-health interest identified in s. 53.

For personal data processed for health research, the Health Research Regulations impose suitable and specific measures, including the current consent/declaration/exception conditions. These are additional measures and do not themselves supply a GDPR Art. 6 basis or replace an Art. 9(2) condition.

items.label: Explicit consent, recorded and retained
items.statement: Valid explicit consent covers the health-research processing, is recorded and retained, and meets current Reg. 3(1)(e), as substituted by S.I. 18/2021 Reg. 4.

items.label: Consent declaration by the Health Research Consent Declaration Committee
items.statement: An applicable Committee consent declaration under Reg. 5 is in force and its conditions are met; the controller has completed the required DPIA and obtained ethics approval before applying. An application alone is insufficient.

items.label: Retrospective chart review (Reg. 3A)
items.statement: All Reg. 3A conditions hold: an eligible internal retrospective study of this controller's care records, qualifying personnel, ethics approval with a written low-risk finding, prescribed notices, no disclosure to another person for the study, and non-identifying published findings.

items.label: Deferred consent, incapacity (Reg. 3B)
items.statement: All Reg. 3B conditions hold: exceptional circumstances, processing principally necessary for care and vital interests of an individual unable to consent, related ethics-approved research, prompt consent when capacity permits, oral/written information including sharing, and the withdrawal/erasure rules and their qualified exception.

items.label: Research begun before 8 August 2018 (Reg. 6; not modelled)
items.statement: The transitional Reg. 6 route, including its amendments and deadlines, is not fully modelled and cannot establish present permission.

requirements.statement: DPA 2018 s. 54, subject to s. 42, supplies a basis for necessary and proportionate special-category research, archiving and statistical processing. Health-research measures apply additionally where their scope is met.
